title: Home Depot (HD) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
transcript:
A CEO handoff and a cut to SRS growth expectations headline the quarter.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

TAKEAWAYS

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email[email protected]

RISKS

SUMMARY

Home Depot(HD-2.45%)reported third quarter results and announced that its interim leadership structure will conclude on Nov. 23, 2026. Management updated its full-year guidance to reflect the impact of recent acquisitions and consistent demand patterns in repair and remodel categories. The company reported that current market conditions remain pressured by high interest rates, though investments in professional services and digital fulfillment contributed to market share gains. Management stated that the core business is currently driven by smaller maintenance and repair projects rather than large-scale renovations.

INDUSTRY GLOSSARY

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator:Greetings, and welcome to The Home Depot Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call.[Operator Instructions]As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. It is now my pleasure to introduce your host, Isabel Janci. Please go ahead.

Isabel Janci:Thank you, Christine, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to The Home Depot's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Joining us on our call today are Ted Decker, Chair; Richard McPhail, incoming Chief Executive Officer; Ann-Marie Campbell, incoming President and Chief Operating Officer; Billy Bastek, Executive Vice President of Merchandising; and Jordan Broggi, incoming Chief Financial Officer. Following our prepared remarks, the call will be open for questions.[Operator Instructions]If we are unable to get to your question during the call, please call our Investor Relations department at (770) 384-2387.

Before I turn the call over to Ted, let me remind you that today's press release and the presentations made by our executives include forward-looking statements under the federal securities laws, including as defined in the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from our expectations and projections. These risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to, the factors identified in the release in our most recent annual report on Form 10-K and in our other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Today's presentation will also include certain non-GAAP measures, including, but not limited to, adjusted operating margin, adjusted diluted earnings per share and return on invested capital. For a reconciliation of these and other non-GAAP measures to our corresponding GAAP measures, please refer to our earnings press release on our Investor Relations website. Now let me turn the call over to Ted.

Edward Decker:Thank you, Isabel, and good morning, everyone. Before the team discusses our results, I want to thank Richard, Anne and our entire team for their outstanding leadership during my leave. I'm glad to be back and grateful for the support I received from our associates, Board, partners and many others across The Home Depot community. The Board and I have agreed that now is the right time to move to the next phase of our succession plan. Effective November 23, 2026, the interim Office of the CEO structure we put in place during my leave will conclude. Richard will become Chief Executive Officer and join our Board of Directors.

Anne will become President and Chief Operating Officer, and I will continue to serve as Chair of our Board. Richard and Anne are tremendous leaders with strong track records of serving our customers, championing our culture, taking care of our associates and executing our strategy. Together, they bring deep operating, financial and strategic experience across The Home Depot as well as a solid business partnership honed over several years of close collaboration. With Richard's 21-year tenure at The Home Depot, he brings strategic vision, operational discipline, financial acumen and a proven track record of delivering results. As a 41-year veteran of The Home Depot, Anne has driven results across a number of strategic roles, including stores, operations, merchandising and marketing.

I have great confidence in Richard and Anne, our leadership team and the future of The Home Depot. With that, I'll turn it over to Richard.

Richard McPhail:Thank you, Ted, and good morning, everyone. On behalf of the entire Home Depot family, I'd first like to thank Ted for his leadership and unwavering dedication to The Home Depot as CEO over the last several years. I would also like to personally thank him for his guidance and support and for our friendship over the past 21 years, and I look forward to his continued counsel as Chair of The Home Depot. I would like to thank Anne for her close partnership and for setting an example of inspiring leadership for all of us over the years.

In addition to having driven operational discipline and success in so many different roles throughout her career, she is one of the greatest culture champions this company has ever had, and I congratulate her for her well-deserved promotion to President and Chief Operating Officer of The Home Depot. We've worked together for over 20 years, and I look forward to driving our next chapter of growth together. I'd also like to congratulate Jordan on his promotion to CFO. Since he joined The Home Depot 13 years ago, Jordan has become a strategic thought leader and results-driven business partner.

Prior to his most recent roles as EVP of Interconnected Retail and President of Online, Jordan spent the majority of his career at The Home Depot in finance, spanning strategic business development, FP&A and merchandising and supply chain finance, culminating in his Senior Vice President of Finance role, where he had responsibility for the day-to-day management of the company's P&L. His depth of knowledge across our entire company will be invaluable as he transitions to the financial stewardship of the company, and I look forward to working with him in his new role. And finally, and most importantly, I would like to recognize all of our fellow orange-blooded associates of The Home Depot.

Their passion, ownership and love for this company are what makes The Home Depot great. And I thank them for all they do every day to protect our culture, stand by our values and take care of our customers. Now I'll turn to the results in the quarter. Sales for the third quarter were $43.4 billion, an increase of 4.9% from the same period last year. Comp sales increased 2.2% from the same period last year, and comps in the U.S. increased 2.2%. Adjusted diluted earnings per share were $3.86 in the third quarter compared to $3.74 in the third quarter last year.

In the U.S., our Northern and Western divisions posted positive comps, and the Southern division was essentially flat. Mexico, Canada and SRS also posted positive comps. Third quarter results exceeded our expectations. We saw broad-based engagement across the business with notable strength in repair and remodel categories. 13 of our 16 merchandising departments posted positive comps, and online continues to deliver double-digit growth. Our results are a testament to our commitment to our strategy, driving our core and culture, delivering a frictionless interconnected experience and winning the Pro. And our investments across the business are resonating with our customers, and we are continuing to gain market share in a pressured housing market. Today, we also updated guidance.

We now expect sales growth of approximately 4.5%, comp growth of approximately 1.4% and adjusted diluted earnings per share growth of approximately 2%. I will discuss this in greater detail in a moment. With that, I'll turn it over to Anne.

Ann-Marie Campbell:Good morning, everyone. As Richard said, we continue to differentiate ourselves through strategic investments across the business. This, together with our team's engagement and ability to execute our strategy, positions us well to grow market share in what remains a dynamic environment. Our focus on core and culture is rooted in the belief that we must deliver exceptional customer service every single day for every single customer. This includes having the right brands, products in stock and available for sale and providing a high degree of service.

Our merchants have done an incredible job curating the best product assortment, both in our stores and online, ensuring we have the right inventory, job lot quantities and innovative products available whenever and wherever our customers choose to shop. At the same time, we are maintaining record levels of on-shelf availability and equipping our Orange Apron associates with the tools and training they need to focus on what matters most, helping customers solve problems and fulfill their dreams. One of our goals is to drive deeper engagement in our specialty departments, so we have enhanced our consultative sales training, combining in-person sessions, structured role-playing and targeted selling techniques to improve the customer experience during complex purchases.

Equally important, we are equipping our store leaders with training to actively reinforce the right customer-first behaviors on the sales floor. We are also focused on continuously elevating our interconnected experience to remove friction and drive engagement, whether a customer is using our app to locate a product in the aisle, picking up an order in store or having items delivered straight to their doorstep. We are delivering a faster, more seamless end-to-end shopping journey that keeps our customers coming back. This quarter is the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit online comp growth.

These results are a direct reflection of the enhancements we have made on our site, including AI-enabled search, targeted marketing, expanded assortment and a faster experience from checkout to delivery. Our stores serve as a critical hub for interconnected fulfillment with over half of our online orders fulfilled through our stores. Today, we offer customers a multitude of fulfillment options from buy online, pick up in store to scheduled job site deliveries to fast home delivery. But when projects are underway, we know that speed is paramount. And I want to take a minute to highlight the incredible momentum we are seeing with express delivery.

Following our nationwide launch 3 months ago, we have seen tremendous adoption and engagement with express delivery. Delivery is available on tens of thousands of products now within 2 hours with the majority of those deliveries arriving in less than 1 hour. For customers using our fast delivery, engagement has increased across all channels. Sales have grown, and customer satisfaction scores have improved. Building on this momentum, we have expanded our express delivery hours and now offer express delivery in virtually all stores. And we are winning with the Pro.

All of our Pro cohorts positively comped in the quarter, including Pros shopping in the store and larger Pros working on complex projects and using more of our ecosystem of capabilities. This success reflects the power of our unified Pro team and our comprehensive services and capabilities for the Pro. In terms of the Pro team, which is led by our Pro customer experience managers in our stores, we are building seamless connectivity between our dedicated in-store Pro desk teams and our outside sales organization. And we are supporting these teams with expanded insights and Pro CRM tools giving our associates more robust project visibility and actionable insight into Pros' ongoing jobs.

By combining these enhancements with capabilities like our AI material list builder, project tools, complex delivery scheduling, trade credit and our Pro Xtra loyalty program, we are removing friction from every buying occasion. This integrated approach is creating a truly sticky relationship with our Pros and enabling us to grow wallet share. In closing, I want to thank all of our associates for their hard work and dedication this quarter. Their passion and commitment to our customers are what makes The Home Depot unique and what enables us to win market share. With that, I'll turn it over to Billy.

William Bastek:Thank you, Anne, and good morning, everyone. I want to start by also thanking all of our associates, supplier and supply chain partners for their ongoing commitment to serving our customers and communities. Our performance during the third quarter exceeded our expectations as customers continue to engage in smaller repair and maintenance projects. In the third quarter, we saw strong engagement across the business with 13 of our 16 merchandising departments posting positive comps, including power, storage, plumbing, electrical, indoor garden, appliances, hardware, building materials, kitchen, paint, lumber, bath and lighting. We saw notable strength in our power department, which posted double-digit positive comps, and across storage, plumbing and electrical, which posted mid-single-digit positive comps.

During the third quarter, our comp average ticket increased 3% and comp transactions decreased 0.5%. Big-ticket comp transactions, or those over $1,000, were positive 4.5% compared to the third quarter of last year. Our big-ticket performance was driven by strength in power and appliances. During the third quarter, Pro and DIY both posted positive comps with Pro outperforming DIY. We saw strength in DIY across a number of categories, including appliances, storage, hardscapes and faucets. And for Pro, we saw strength across many Pro-heavy categories like portable power, pipe and fittings, water heaters, insulation, siding, irrigation, fasteners and hand tools. Turning to total company online comp sales.

Sales leveraging our digital platforms increased approximately 13% compared to the third quarter of last year. Our continued success in online is driven by our ongoing investments from site speed to AI-enabled search to a multitude of fulfillment options, including our express delivery, all of which are working together to improve the interconnected experience, driving greater conversion and higher sales growth. During the third quarter, we leaned into products and projects that are resonating with our customers. We focused on innovation, expanded assortments and reduced friction points, all to deliver a compelling value proposition. We continue to see tremendous success in our power business.

As we've mentioned before, we have built a strong competitive advantage with our extensive lineup of battery-powered platforms that allows us to continue to grow share in these categories. Our nearly 2,000 exclusive SKUs across our battery platforms from power tools to outdoor power equipment to lifestyle and recreational products create a unique loyalty program. And another category where we saw strength was plumbing. The team consistently enhances shopability, whether online or in our aisles, focused on expanding assortment and bringing innovation to our customers across categories such as air circulation, water heaters and plumbing repair items.

And in appliances, the investments we have made to improve the shopping experience for our customers and increase speed and delivery for critical direct purchases are contributing to our strength in the category. Over the last 3 months, we have expanded our next-day coverage on key SKUs from nearly 60% of the U.S. population to nearly 85% of the U.S. population. During the third quarter, we also hosted our annual supplier partnership meeting, where we always focus on how to more effectively work with our vendors to bring the best products to market, deliver innovative solutions that simplify the project and offer great value with best-in-class features and benefits.

At the event, we recognized a number of vendors across categories who continue to transform the industry with the innovation they bring to our customers on a daily basis. They included Delta, Behr, Milwaukee, Ryobi, DEWALT, Diablo, USG, Kohler, Levolor and many more. Turning to the fourth quarter. We are looking forward to the excitement we will bring this year with our annual holiday, Black Friday and gift center events. In our gift center event, we continue to lean into brands that matter most for our customers with our assortment of Milwaukee, Ryobi, Makita, DEWALT, RIDGID, Diablo, Husky and more. And in appliances for Black Friday, we have exciting offers on LG, Samsung, Bosch, Whirlpool, GE and Frigidaire.

And in our Smart Home business, we're delivering compelling value with top national brands like Ring, Google, Blink, Echo and Govee. Our true point of differentiation is our proprietary Hubspace platform now active in millions of households. Built to simplify whole home connectivity in a single app, Hubspace has over 280 connected items spanning core home improvement products, including ceiling fans, lighting, bath fans, electrical outlets and many more. We are also accelerating adoption through trusted national partners, highlighted by this week's online launch of our new Kwikset Smart Lock powered by Hubspace. And heading into the holidays, we brought Hubspace directly into our viral Grand Duchess tree collection, giving customers seamless app-controlled lighting right out of the box.

As we look ahead to the fourth quarter, our merchandising organization remains focused on being our customers' advocate for value. This means continuing to provide a broad assortment of best-in-class products that are in stock and available for our customers when they need it. With that, I'd like to turn the call back over to Richard.

Richard McPhail:Thanks, Billy. I'll now spend a few minutes on our financial update for the quarter. In the third quarter, total sales were $43.4 billion, an increase of $2 billion or 4.9% from last year. During the third quarter, our total company comps were positive 2.2%, with comps of positive 1.1% in August, positive 3.8% in September and positive 1.8% in October. Comps in the U.S. were positive 2.2% for the quarter, with comps of positive 1.1% in August, positive 4.4% in September and positive 1.3% in October.

In the third quarter, our gross margin was 32.8%, a decrease of approximately 60 basis points from the third quarter of last year, reflecting a rising cost environment as well as a change in mix as a result of acquisitions. During the third quarter, operating expense as a percent of sales decreased approximately 30 basis points to 20.1% compared to the third quarter of 2025. Our operating expense performance was in line with our expectations. Our operating margin for the third quarter was 12.6% compared to 12.9% in the third quarter of 2025. In the quarter, pretax intangible asset amortization was $182 million.

Excluding the intangible asset amortization in the quarter, our adjusted operating margin for the third quarter was 13% compared to 13.3% in the third quarter of 2025. Interest and other expense for the third quarter decreased by $68 million to $528 million. In the third quarter, our effective tax rate was 25% compared to 24.3% in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Our diluted earnings per share for the third quarter were $3.72 compared to $3.62 in the third quarter of 2025. Excluding intangible asset amortization, our adjusted diluted earnings per share for the third quarter were $3.86, an increase of 3.2% compared to the third quarter of 2025.

During the third quarter, we opened 8 net new stores, bringing our total store count to 2,372. At the end of the quarter, merchandise inventories were $27.6 billion, up approximately $1.4 billion compared to the third quarter of 2025, and inventory turns were 4.4x, down from 4.5x last year. Turning to capital allocation. During the third quarter, we invested approximately $955 million back into our business in the form of capital expenditures. And during the quarter, we paid approximately $2.3 billion in dividends to our shareholders. Computed on the average of beginning and ending long-term debt and equity for the trailing 12 months, return on invested capital was 24.5%, down from 26.3% in the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

Now I will comment on our outlook for fiscal 2026. We are encouraged with the underlying demand and continued share gains we see across the business. With 1 quarter remaining, we are updating our guidance for fiscal 2026. We now expect total sales growth of approximately 4.5%, reflecting comparable sales growth of approximately 1.4% for the year and the contribution of the GMS acquisition, new stores, new branches and tuck-in acquisitions. For the year, we expect SRS to deliver low single-digit percent organic sales growth. We plan to open approximately 15 new stores and 40 to 50 new SRS branches. Our gross margin is expected to be approximately 33%.

Further, we expect operating margin of approximately 12.4% and adjusted operating margin of approximately 12.8%. Our effective tax rate is targeted at approximately 24.6%. We expect net interest expense of approximately $2.2 billion. We expect our diluted earnings per share to increase approximately 1.5% compared to fiscal 2025. We expect adjusted diluted earnings per share to increase approximately 2% compared to fiscal 2025. We plan to continue investing in our business with capital expenditures of approximately 2.5% of sales for fiscal 2026. We believe that we will continue to grow market share as a result of our competitive advantages and ongoing investments by delivering the best customer experience in home improvement. Thank you for your participation in today's call.

And Christine, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:[Operator Instructions]Our first question comes from the line of Christopher Horvers with JPMorgan.

Christopher Horvers:Congratulations to everyone on their new roles. Ted, it's really great to hear your voice again. And congratulations on the next phase of your career and your life as well. And so my first question is -- my first question is, as you think about the underlying trends in the business, how are you thinking about it? Every quarter has noise, was weather a net helper as extended warmth in the U.S. in many regions, but you also didn't have a great storm season.

So as you think about this doing nearly 2% in the back half of the year based on what you're implying for the fourth quarter, is that the right launching point for '27 that we could potentially build from? Or are you concerned at all about any lagged negative impact from the run-up in mortgage rates?

Richard McPhail:So Chris, it's Richard. I'll turn it over to Billy in a minute. First of all, I'd say we have seen really steady demand patterns in this business when you factor out some of the influences that you alluded to and Billy will talk about. As far as 2027 goes, again, we've had steady demand patterns in this business. We've learned it's better to be able to manage with agility rather than to try to be great at predicting. And we have established that track record over time. So we're extremely pleased with the quarter. But Billy, maybe talk a little bit about timing nuances there in kind of Q3, Q4.

William Bastek:Yes. Thanks, Chris, for the question. As Richard mentioned, the underlying demand, we feel great about, and we can go back to Q2 and some of the things that we talked about there relative to kind of the core of our business, which we feel great about. So the underlying demand remains really consistent. We talked about some of the categories where we had some outperformance in categories like all of our power business, think electrical and plumbing. There's always some seasonal aspects. I mean we had a much warmer September as one example. So we sold some more ACs and fans during that month.

And you see in the monthly cadence, you can see between that and the Labor Day shift, you can see a little outperformance there. But the key that we spend our energy on is obviously watching the underlying demand, and we feel great about the interaction we see from our customers. Maintenance and repair is certainly driving our business as it was back in the Q2 area. And so we feel really good about the underlying demand and what we can control and candidly, the share that we're taking along the way.

Christopher Horvers:Got it. And then on the outlook on the operating margin side, you took the sales outlook to the high end and the operating margin is going to the lower end. So can you talk about what was different relative to your expectations? It looks like you made another acquisition during the quarter. How much of it is that? And then as you think about the exit, the 12.8%, is that the right launching point as you think about '27 in light of lapping tariff headwinds, but persistent energy cost pressures that you won't annualize until the back half?

Richard McPhail:Thanks, Chris. So first, I just want to give a huge shout-out to Billy's merchandising team and John Deaton's supply chain team for managing the business as well as they have through years, not just 2026, but years of what you call a unique cost environment. They have continued to do that through 2026. When you look at our guide, yes, despite increasing pressures in our market, we're pleased that our guide is actually north of our midpoint of the original guidance. As Billy alluded to, we think that the market is much softer now than we had expected at the beginning of the year.

And so we look at that and feel very confident that we're taking share because of our investments and the great work of our teams. When you look at operating margin guidance, that is solely driven by a slight change in gross margin outlook, and that is driven simply by a change in product mix. We've had some strength in categories that are accretive to sales and accretive to earnings, but just carry a different margin. And Chris, you're right, we made a few acquisitions during the year, notably building up our HVAC vertical at SRS. And so that sort of tipped the margin guidance down to the lower level. But again, we feel great about the guide.

And just on the adjusted EPS guide of 2%, that also had a little bit of pressure from tax rate where we saw fewer positive discrete items, not a lot in that. I think that the message to take away is we're running the business exactly the way that we want to. We've got great steady momentum with our customer, and we're taking share.

Operator:Our next question comes from the line of Steven Zaccone with Citi. Our next question comes from the line of Zhihan Ma with Bernstein.

Zhihan Ma:My first one is, you've been talking about this market share gains, especially on the retail side, especially since last quarter. Could you share some of the specific initiatives behind what's driving your market share gains?

Richard McPhail:Well, I'm going to -- I'll start here just with a recap of everything we're happy about because we really do feel like we're clicking on so many cylinders. And I'm going to turn it over to Anne and to Billy here in a minute. But the performance is not by accident. It's built on a strategy that Ted created and we refined for years and an investment program designed to win share in any economic environment. I mean just look at the quarter, we posted our highest comp sales growth in 4 years. We had positive comp across most U.S. regions, Canada, Mexico and SRS.

We had positive comps in most departments with real outlier performance in areas we've leaned into, and Billy will talk about that. Our investments in express delivery and in AI customer and associate enablement are making a meaningful difference in customer satisfaction and conversion. By the way, we posted the highest online comp in 5 years this quarter. And our investments in Pro are paying off. We posted 9 quarters in a row of positive comp in sales to Pro customers. It really all starts in the store and enabling our stores and associates. And so Anne, maybe we start there.

Ann-Marie Campbell:Yes. No, thank you. Just #1, I just want to thank all the associates for what they do every single day. And to Richard's point, it starts with them. And so we have continued to make investments. Over the last couple of years, we've talked about the investment in training, first of all, just how do we get our associates to really engage with the customer. And we have this framework, we call it GET: Greet, Engage and Thank. And over the last couple of years, we have even shifted to an email survey and our data tells us we are getting better and better with driving engagement across the board. Engagement matters because engagement drives conversion.

So making sure that our associates are engaged is really, really important. I also highlighted the next stage of what we have done with our consultative part of the business, where we are taking all our specialists. These are the guys and gals who really deal with complex purchases, and we're investing in training for them so that they can continue to kind of drive the level of engagement and experience our customers expect. We tested that in 2 regions across the company a year ago and it yields tremendous benefit. And so we're going to continue to roll that out. So the training component is there around the engagement.

But I don't want to underestimate to you the investments we have made with our visual intelligence and driving product availability and on-shelf availability. It starts with product. We know the innovation that Billy brings to the table every single day. We talk about the engagement. But at the end of the day, we need to have the depth of product to drive the conversion with our Pros and our consumer. And as we lean into delivery, just think about that, where our stores are, we have always said our real estate is a competitive advantage. And by gosh, it's proven to be even a better competitive advantage as we lean into complex delivery.

So the investments are working across our entire portfolio. And last but not least, I mentioned in my prepared comments that all Pro cohorts are positive comping. And we have talked about the investment we've made in leadership. We've talked about the investment we've made in tools. And now as we continue to drive that level of connectivity and that level of adoption, we are seeing outsized benefits in some of those areas as well. So core and culture, interconnected and win with the Pro.

And I'm glad to see the associates and our leaders just taking advantage of that and really delivering for us, not only in the third quarter, but what we expect in the fourth quarter and beyond.

Zhihan Ma:That's really helpful. And just a follow-up on the strong ticket growth that you're seeing. Could you help us understand how much of that is -- I mean, maybe people are buying more per basket from a Pro or online perspective? And how much of that is just you managing the cost inflation environment and passing on some of that cost inflation?

William Bastek:Yes. Thanks, Zhihan. I'll take that. So there's a couple of components to that. Certainly, there's been some modest price we've talked about taken, but it's really kind of split. We look at the category mix and not only the category mix, but the intra-category mix. So it's kind of a 50-50 breakout in terms of the AUR piece. So we've seen great engagement as we've talked about, but we also -- from a category mix standpoint and then inside those categories, you think about something like power tools and how we see people trade up inside of that, you think about appliances and the same thing.

So you've got category mix as a portion of that and then that intra-category mix along with, like I said, taking some of the modest price that we've talked about previously.

Operator:Our next question comes from the line of Steven Zaccone with Citi.

Steven Zaccone:Hopefully, you guys can hear me. Apologies for that. Congrats everybody on their recent appointments. It is nice to hear from you again, Ted. My question is on SRS. So it sounds like there was a slight change. We're expecting low single-digit growth versus the prior plan for mid-singles. So could you just talk a little bit about that? Any callouts by specific vertical within SRS as well? There wasn't much of a storm season. So curious if you could talk about some of the verticals there.

Richard McPhail:Right. And you really hit it on the head there. I mean we feel incredible about -- as Anne said, our entire enterprise Pro efforts, right? And I'll let Mike Rowe talk a little bit about what we're seeing across enterprise in a second. Specifically with respect to SRS, they delivered almost $5 billion in sales in the quarter, and they delivered positive total sales growth and positive comp sales growth. When you look at the pressure in the roofing market now, you'd have to say it's almost unprecedented. We've had 2 years in a row with really very little storm seasons that are really part of the normal demand pattern for roofing.

So the new updated guidance for SRS is purely a reflection of those roofing-oriented categories where there's just enormous pressure. Everything else, we're just so pleased with performance across the rest of the verticals. And so you would say this is isolated. We also are confident that we are taking material share from the market and from competition. And the value prop we're creating across SRS and then across SRS and The Home Depot is unique to the market, and we're seeing great traction there. Mike, maybe you just expand on that a little bit.

Michael Rowe:Yes. Sure, Richard. And Anne touched on a bunch of it as well. We continue to see great success from the investment that we've made in the Pro ecosystem. As we invest in those capabilities and improve the experience with Pros, we're getting a greater share of wallet from our Pros and see more growth. When you think about it, for instance, the initial discovery and ordering, we continue to invest in our B2B experience, which is giving us outsized growth online because of capabilities like project planning, material lists, customer account dashboards and more.

And then you think about for executing the orders, we're investing in order management and delivery that Anne talked about, specifically with things like self-service site instructions, our customer business hours availability, along with more improvements in delivery tracking and all leading to the highest levels of on-time and complete and customer satisfaction scoring. And we continue to lean into excellence in delivery and faster and faster delivery, as Anne pointed out. As I noted, these capabilities and more, they continue to allow us to earn more wallet share with our Pros. And it's just a solid combination of a better in-store, better online and on-the-job-site experience improvements letting us take share.

And Steven, maybe to tie in more to your question around the cross-sell, too, back with SRS, we're on track to meet the $400 million goal that we laid out for 2026, and we look to double that in '27. Our cross-category efforts have been accelerating with more categories awarded to us from customers who used to buy more singular categories. So working together across our companies, Home Depot, SRS, HD Supply and CR, we can bring a pretty unique value proposition to the Pro and maximize the share of wallet that can be served by The Home Depot.

Steven Zaccone:Great. The follow-up I had was just on the gross margin outlook for the fourth quarter. I understand you gave some earlier comments as it relates to product mix. But I was curious if you could just opine a bit more on your updated expectations for 4Q. It was a little bit worse than where the Street was previously. Is there anything else to call out in terms of promotional backdrop that you're seeing? Just curious for any more color.

Richard McPhail:Yes. I'll turn to Billy here in a second. But really, the fourth quarter will be a little lower than last year. This is reflected in our updated guidance for gross margin and operating margin. And that simply reflects, again, mix effect, product mix and also a little bit of mix from acquisitions. And so again, Billy and his team have done an incredible job over the last several years managing through a cost environment that is certainly challenging. Billy, maybe just give a little bit of color on that.

William Bastek:Yes. I mean, obviously, we've had the incrementality of some of the things we talked about last quarter, from a guide standpoint that was not in our projections for 2026, and we have worked through those -- the teams have worked through those really, really well. And candidly, we had more volatility in 2025 than we do in 2026. As it pertains to Q4, as Richard mentioned, we do have some different mix orientation as it just relates to the seasonality of the businesses and certainly the weather in the North. But we feel really strong about the value that we have in the marketplace.
